variants.when: Many Saturns, for example the 2005–2010 VUE: accelerator pedal method
steps: Reset only after the engine oil and filter have actually been changed.
Turn the key to RUN (ON) with the engine off.
Push the accelerator pedal all the way down and let it up three times within five seconds.
The change oil light flashes or goes out to show the reset worked.
If the light comes back on and stays on at the next key-on, repeat the steps.

variants.when: Saturns with a Driver Information Center, such as the 2009 AURA and SKY or an OUTLOOK with DIC buttons
steps: Reset only after the engine oil and filter have actually been changed.
Turn the ignition on with the engine off and the vehicle in Park.
Use the DIC buttons to reach the oil life screen (on the AURA and SKY, press the information and reset buttons together and scroll to OIL LIFE RESET).
Press and hold the reset (set/reset) button until 100% or ACKNOWLEDGED shows.
Turn the ignition off and check that the oil message does not return at the next start.

variants.when: Saturns that show oil life in the odometer display, such as the 2005 ION or an OUTLOOK without DIC buttons
steps: Reset only after the engine oil and filter have actually been changed.
Press the trip odometer reset stem until the oil life display shows.
Press and hold the stem until the oil life reads 100% or the chimes sound.
If the oil message comes back at the next start, repeat the steps.

variants.when: Late-model Saturns with a low tire pressure light (for example the 2009 AURA and SKY and the 2010 VUE)
steps: Set all four tires to the cold pressure on the Tire and Loading Information label on the driver's side (cold means parked three hours or driven under a mile).
There is no reset button. The light stays on until the pressure is corrected, then goes off on its own.
Clearing the CHECK TIRE PRESSURE message only hides it until the next start if a tire is still low.
variants.note: If the light flashes for about a minute and then stays on, the system has a fault that adding air will not fix. After a tire rotation the sensors must be matched to their new positions.

notes: Saturn used the GM Oil Life System, so the reminder is based on how the engine is used, not a fixed mileage. The reset method depends on the model and year: the accelerator pedal method, the Driver Information Center buttons, or the trip odometer stem.
